## Iteration 623 — Receipt and return ready for the next scan (2026-11-09)

### Capability matrix rescan (cooler of units coming back or arriving)

After a ward receipt or return was recorded, Unit number still held the unit just done, its issue stayed selected, and nothing had the focus. Scanning the next unit in the cooler meant clicking the field and clearing it first. The submit button stayed live on the finished unit, so a second press sent it again (the server refused it, but the bench saw an error instead of a ready form). The ward form also kept the received unit's notices.

### Design

- Ward receipt success: the unit (issue id, Unit number, its notices) is cleared; Received by stays for the rest of the cooler; Unit number takes the focus (Cycle 622's focus mechanism).
- Return success: issue id and Unit number cleared (the reason already stays while more of the shipment is out; each unit is inspected again); Unit number takes the focus.
- Acknowledge receipt, Check status, and Return unit are disabled until a unit is chosen.

### Verification

- Rendered flows: a return and a ward receipt each leave Unit number empty, the button disabled, and the focus on Unit number (both fail without the change).
- Live (read-only; no receipt or return recorded on dev data): Ward receipt and Return open with the cursor in Unit number and Acknowledge receipt / Return unit disabled until a unit is chosen. The after-save behaviour is shown by the rendered flows. No server errors. The focus check reads the page's own field reference: bUnit does not keep the reference attribute on every render, which first made the check look at nothing.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-667, FRS-BB-784.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-746, TEST-BB-747.

### Next

- Transfusion documentation runs per unit at the bedside: check the same after Start and Complete (what stays, what clears, where the focus goes).

## Iteration 624 — The bedside reaction answer binds; the finished unit leaves the form (2026-11-09)

### Capability matrix rescan (Transfusion desk: Start, Complete, Document)

Writing a rendered test for Complete found a defect far worse than the planned one: the "Transfusion reaction suspected?" select (Cycle 596) could never take an answer. It bound a `bool?` with options valued `@false` and `@true`. Blazor renders those as no value attribute (the browser then sends the option's text, "No reaction") and an empty one (sent as unanswered), and a select's binder for a bool casts the checkbox's true or false, so even correct text would not bind. Live: the options read "No reaction" (no value) and "" (Yes). Every Complete transfusion and Document start and finish on Issue & Transfuse was refused with "Say whether a transfusion reaction is suspected" since Cycle 596. Cycle 596's tests covered the server refusal and a source check against checkboxes, not the select taking an answer.

The planned item stood too: after Complete or Document, the finished unit stayed on the form with its buttons live and nothing focused.

### Design

- The select binds through text: "no", "yes", or "" map to false, true, or unanswered. Same question and options.
- After Complete or Document: the unit (issue id, Unit number, its notices) is cleared and Unit number takes the focus; the patient, the identifiers, and the transfusionist entered at this bedside stay. Start keeps the unit (Complete follows).
- A unit scanned during a bedside run opens as the run's Next button does, so the same patient's identifiers stay.
- Start, Document, and Complete are disabled with no unit.
- Source test: no option value is a C# boolean literal, and no select is bound to a bool field (it catches the original code).

### Verification

- Rendered flow: the reaction answer binds; Complete succeeds; Unit number is empty and focused; Start and Document are disabled; scanning the patient's next unit opens it with the identifier kept. Fails on the original select.
- Live (read-only; nothing completed): before the fix the options read value "" (Yes) and no value ("No reaction"); after it, "", "no", "yes", and "No reaction" stays chosen when another field re-renders the form. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-668, FRS-BB-785.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-748, TEST-BB-749.

### Next

- Look for other forms whose required answer is only checked server-side and never exercised by a rendered test that fills it in: a value that cannot bind looks the same as one left blank.

## Iteration 625 — Every required select proved to bind (2026-11-09)

### Capability matrix rescan (answers that cannot bind)

After Cycle 624 every select on every page was listed with the type of the field it binds. Each type was run through Blazor's own converter: "" is unanswered and every option's rendered value converts to its answer. A bool is the one that does not: the converter throws on the cast, which is what Cycle 624 fixed. Radio buttons on the worklist use explicit handlers. No other answer that cannot bind was found.

- TEST-BB-751: bool? throws on a select's text; the text form binds.
- The Cycle 624 source test already refuses a select bound to a bool and boolean literal option values.

- URS-BB-668 / FRS-BB-785 (verification only).

### Tests

- TEST-BB-750, TEST-BB-751.

## Iteration 626 — Bedside warned of a reaction under investigation (2026-11-09)

### Capability matrix rescan (after a suspected reaction)

With the reaction answer binding again (Cycle 624), the "Yes, reaction suspected" path was walked. The server opens the investigation and the form links to it. But the Transfusion desk, after Cycle 624, empties the unit and waits for the next scan, and the bedside run offers Next for the same patient: nothing on the desk said that patient's reaction was still under investigation. The recorded-reaction banner is on the chart only, and the investigations list needs the reaction-investigate permission bedside staff may not hold. Practice is to stop and evaluate before transfusing again; whether the LIS should block that is a clinical decision, recorded as OCD-078, so this warns.

### Design

- `ReactionInvestigationService.OpenByPatientAsync`: per patient, the latest investigation open or under review.
- The outstanding list carries it on each of the patient's units (`OpenReactionInvestigationId`, `OpenReactionReportedUtc`), readable by anyone who can see Issued units.
- Issued units: a red "Reaction under investigation" badge on the patient's units.
- Transfusion desk: an amber warning above the form for the chosen unit's patient, or the bedside run's patient once the finished unit has left the form, with the number and report time, "Do not start another unit unless the physician has decided to continue", and a link for those who can open investigations. Start and Document stay available.

### Verification

- Integration: open and under-review investigations are carried, a closed one and another patient's are not. Rendered: the badge on the patient's unit, the warning on the desk with the number, Start still enabled, and no warning for another patient's unit.
- Live (read-only): Issued units loads without server errors; no demo patient with a unit out has a reaction under investigation, so no badge shows on dev data (the demo reaction case has no unit outstanding).

### Requirements

- URS-BB-669, FRS-BB-786, OCD-078.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-752, TEST-BB-753.

### Next

- Check whether issuing a new unit to a patient with a reaction under investigation says so on Ready to issue and the issue form, before the unit leaves the bank.

## Iteration 627 — Issue desk warned of a reaction under investigation (2026-11-09)

### Capability matrix rescan (issue after a suspected reaction)

Cycle 626 warned the bedside; the bank itself still issued the patient's next reserved unit with nothing said. Ready to issue and the Issue form now say so before the unit leaves.

Writing the rendered test found a latent fault: Issue on a Ready to issue row switched to the Issue desk and focused its form in the same click. The form had not rendered yet, so the focus threw ("ElementReference has not been configured correctly"). It worked live only because the special-requirements request in between yielded and let the form render; any path that completed without yielding (a patient without an id, a cached answer) would have thrown in the click, which on Blazor Server ends the user's session.

### Design

- `ReadyToIssueWorkItemDto.OpenReactionInvestigationId` / `OpenReactionReportedUtc` from the Cycle 626 lookup.
- Ready to issue: a red "Reaction under investigation" badge on the patient's reserved units.
- Issue form: for its patient, an amber warning with the number and report time, "Confirm the physician has decided to continue before issuing another unit." Warning only (OCD-078).
- The Issue form is focused after it renders (both from a row and from Issue next in a run).

### Verification

- Integration: the patient's reserved unit carries the investigation; another patient's does not. Rendered: the badge, the form warning after Issue on the row (and the click no longer throws), none for another patient.
- Live (read-only): Ready to issue loads its 5 demo rows with no badge (no demo patient with a reserved unit has a reaction under investigation) and the Issue desk opens without an error; no demo row is issuable, so Issue on a row is shown by the rendered test. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-670, FRS-BB-787.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-754, TEST-BB-755.

### Next

- Look for other element focuses called in the same handler that changes what is rendered (a desk, a tab, a panel opened in the click) and move them after the render.

## Iteration 628 — Focus after the render (2026-11-09)

### Capability matrix rescan (focus timing)

Every element-reference focus was listed. Delivery receipt, the Inventory retype scan, the scan desks, sign-in's first field, and Patients' search already focus in `OnAfterRenderAsync` with a check that the element is on the page. Sign-in's Password is always rendered. One more relied on timing, like Cycle 627's Issue form: when the password is accepted with an authenticator challenge, sign-in showed the code field and focused it in the same handler (`StateHasChanged()` then `FocusAsync`). The catch covered only a JavaScript error, not the unset reference. It works when the render happens before the focus; a rendered test that completes the request without yielding throws "ElementReference has not been configured correctly", which on the sign-in screen would end the session for anyone using an authenticator.

### Design

- Sign-in sets a flag; the code field is focused in `OnAfterRenderAsync` once it is on the page.
- Source test: an element-reference `FocusAsync` outside `OnAfterRenderAsync` must be on a short list of elements always on their page (sign-in's Password). It fails on the old sign-in code and would have caught Cycle 627's Issue form.

### Verification

- Rendered: the password accepted with a challenge shows the code field and focuses it; the old code throws in the same test.
- Live (read-only; no password entered): sign-in renders with the cursor in Username and no error. The code-field step is shown by the rendered test. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-671, FRS-BB-788.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-756, TEST-BB-757.

### Next

## Iteration 633 — Unit expiry in local time; yes/no selects that could not be chosen (2026-11-09)

### Capability matrix rescan (time display and choices, again)

Planned: record on the issue that the patient's reaction was under investigation. Reading the product history for it found Expires formatted from `UnitExpiresUtc is DateTime unitExpires` without conversion. The sweep found eight such: unit expiration on Ready to issue, Retrospective, In transit, Issued units, the chart's Products and Product History (at UTC−5 a unit expiring 14:00 local read 19:00, five hours later than it does), a specimen's expiry on Compatibility, and Test History's entered time. The Cycle 604 guard looks for members named …Utc and missed a value renamed by the pattern match.

Writing the new guard showed Cycle 624's guard silently broken (and the new one, as first written): a "\b" written through a script became a backspace character, so Cycle 624's "no select bound to a bool" pattern matched nothing. Repaired, it found three more selects bound to a plain bool, which, like Cycle 624's, can never take a choice (the binder casts a checkbox's true or false):
- Storage temperatures "Excursions only": the filter could not be turned on.
- HL7 Translations import "Replace the rows below": an import meant to replace the table added to it.
- HL7 Translations "Test a value" Outbound: outbound could not be checked.

### Design

- The eight renderings convert to local time; values the text labels UTC (backups, reaction closed and reopened) stay.
- The three selects bind through text, as the bedside reaction question.
- Source test: a `…Utc` value matched into a variable is not formatted without `.ToLocalTime()` or `ClockText` unless labelled UTC. Both guards were checked against reintroduced faults (they fail) and the whole tree scanned for control characters (none left).
- The issue-record traceability moves to the next iteration.

### Verification

- Guards fail on the old code (unit expiry, select bound to the reaction bool) and pass now. Converter: a plain bool also throws on a select's text. Rendered: Excursions only is taken and dropped.
- Live (read-only; workstation America/New_York): Ready to issue shows W000123RXN0001 expiring 2026-11-30 21:05, as its unit page does (before: the stored UTC, 02:05 the next day). Temperature history keeps "Excursions only" across a re-render. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-675, FRS-BB-792.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-766, TEST-BB-767 (TEST-BB-749 repaired, TEST-BB-751 extended).

### Next

- Record on each issue the patient's reaction investigation open at the time, and show it in Product History.

## Iteration 641 — Rest 0 per panel phase (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (antibody identification, reaction entry)

Walked the antigram. Each cell and phase is its own grade list (typeable: 0, 1, 2, m, H), so an 11-cell panel read at IS, 37C and AHG is 33 picks, most of them 0. A panel is read one phase at a time. Nothing let the technologist record "the rest of this phase was negative" once the reacting cells were graded.

### Design

- Each interpretive phase heading offers **Rest 0** while that phase has cells at NT and the workup is editable. It sets only those cells to 0 in the form; graded cells and other phases are untouched.
- Cells set that way are outlined, with a note giving the count and asking the technologist to check each against its tube. Changing a cell by hand removes its outline; Save reactions saves and audits them like any grade and clears the outlines.
- Whether this aid is allowed, and for which phases or roles, is a laboratory decision: OCD-079. Completed or voided workups offer none. There is no check-cell column on the antigram (phases are IS, 37C, AHG), so a check cell cannot be set negative this way.

### Safety (question 6)

A cell set to 0 without reading its tube could rule out an antibody. The aid fills only cells still NT, outlines every cell it set until saved, and says to check each; nothing is saved without Save reactions; the audit is unchanged.

### Verification

- Rendered: Rest 0 at IS fills two NT cells and leaves the 2+ cell and the 37C and AHG phases alone; a hand change removes one outline; saving clears them; a completed workup offers none.
- Live (read-only): no open workup exists on development data, and opening one would change it, so the antigram was checked in rendered tests only.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-683, FRS-BB-800, OCD-079.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-780, TEST-BB-781, TEST-BB-782.

### Next

- Continue antibody identification: the interpretation step, and whether a demo workup with reactions in progress should be seeded so the antigram can be walked live.

## Iteration 643 — A typed specificity shows as it will post (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (antibody identification, interpretation)

Checked the worklist's "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" times first: 58 tables use that form, and the guard requires only that a time carry its day, so it is not a defect. Then walked the interpretation. The technologist picks each antibody from the catalog or types it. Typed text was always listed as "free-text; will not drive antigen-negative unless resolved", but on save the server resolves it against the catalog (`AntibodyIdentificationCatalogResolver`) and posts "anti-k" as the catalog anti-K. The page said one thing and the record another; a technologist could also re-pick an antibody believing the typed one would not drive selection.

### Design

- Add specificity resolves typed text with the same domain resolver and the active catalog the page already loads. One match is queued as that catalog antibody and marked "(catalog)"; no match, or text naming more than one antibody, stays as typed and is marked "(not in the catalog; will not drive antigen-negative selection)".
- No server change: the server resolves the same way on save, so what is listed is what posts.

### Safety (question 6)

An identified antibody that the technologist believes is not in the catalog could be re-entered or left unresolved; one that is truly outside the catalog will not drive antigen-negative selection, and the label now says so without the hedge. The server's ABID-INTERP-UNMATCHED warning for an unmatched identified antibody is unchanged.

### Verification

- Rendered: "anti-k" is listed as "anti-K — Identified (catalog)"; "anti-Vel" and "anti-K anti-E" stay as typed and are marked as outside the catalog.
- Live (read-only): on the demo workup (MRN0004), typing "anti-k" and Add specificity lists "anti-K — Identified (catalog)"; reloaded without recording, nothing saved. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-685, FRS-BB-802.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-785, TEST-BB-786.

### Next

- Supervisor review of an antibody workup: what the reviewer must look up elsewhere before accepting.

## Iteration 644 — Supervisor review says who may accept, before the click (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (antibody identification, supervisor review)

Walked supervisor review on the demo workup (in progress, no interpretation). The review card offered Accept and Reject although nothing had been interpreted; the service refuses that (ABID interpretation not recorded). And the technologist who recorded an interpretation, holding the override permission, saw Accept enabled; the service refuses that too when review is required and self-review is blocked (OCD-021). Both were found only after the click.

### Design

- With no technologist interpretation, the review card says "Waiting for the technologist interpretation" and offers neither button.
- The page reads Require supervisor review and Block self-review through the existing read-only policy endpoint, whose allowlist now includes both keys. When both are on and the signed-in user is the interpreting technologist (case-insensitive, as the service compares), the card says another supervisor must accept and disables Accept. Reject stays available, as the service allows it. An unreadable policy counts as on, the shipped default.
- The service checks are unchanged; the page only says beforehand what the service would refuse.

### Verification

- Rendered: no interpretation waits with no buttons; the interpreting technologist (any case) sees the note with Accept disabled and Reject enabled; another supervisor, or the technologist with self-review allowed, may accept.
- Live (read-only): the demo workup's review card waits; the policy endpoint returns both keys.

## Iteration 645 — Complete says what it waits for (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (antibody identification, completion)

## Iteration 650 — Receive the drawn tube, do not draw again (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (patient-product workflows: preparing blood orders)

Walked Blood orders to prepare on development data. Both demo orders said "None usable · Collect a specimen". But Demo-Multi, Riley (MRN0022) has ACC-DEMO-RCV1 drawn on the ward and waiting to be received (Cycle 638): the worklist counted only received or accepted tubes, so it sent the bench to the accession form to draw again. An unneeded second draw for a patient who may be bleeding, and a duplicate tube to reconcile.

### Design

- `BloodOrderPreparationRule.ReceiveInstead`: with no usable specimen, or one that expires before the order is needed, and a tube drawn and not yet received, the next step is "Receive tube {accession}", linked to Pending specimens where the tube is scanned.

- A tube that has expired, or would expire before the order is needed, does not count. Nothing about reserving changes: units are still reserved on a received and accepted specimen with a completed type and screen.

- Unit: receive with no usable specimen or one expiring early; a lasting usable specimen still reserves; blank accession is no tube; nothing left, no step; the link.
- Integration: an in-date drawn tube gives "Receive tube ACC-TR-1" to Pending specimens; an expired tube, or one expiring before needed-by, leaves "Collect a specimen".
- Live (read-only): Riley's ORD-SURG-DEMO says "Receive tube ACC-DEMO-RCV1"; Patricia's order, with no tube, still says collect.

## Iteration 654 — A duplicate EHR order reaches the bench (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (safety rules: duplicate testing; operations: alerts)

Surveyed alerts whose text never depends on the patient: chart headers on four patients now show only patient-specific alerts (Cycle 653 removed the facility-wide electronic crossmatch one); the issue desk's electronic crossmatch note is informational and relevant there. Then walked duplicate testing. A test ordered at the bench that the patient already has open warns (`ORD-DUP-TEST`). ## Iteration 655 — Expiry and record times shown in local time (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (EHR product orders, alerts inbox, time display)

EHR orders arrive as test orders only (the ORM handler builds one test line), so duplicate EHR product orders do not arise; nothing to do there. Walked the Alerts inbox: 20 open, with seven reagent QC lots and eight near-expiry units listed one per row (grouping noted for next). The page headed its times "Raised (UTC)" but showed local times, and its acknowledged and cleared times were stored UTC shown unconverted and unlabelled. The local-time guard (TEST-BB-766) checks a stored time matched into a variable (`x.FooUtc is DateTime t`) only on the same line; here the variable is used inside the @if block on the next line.

### Design

- The guard looks at the matched line and the four after it, and accepts `t.ToString("…") UTC` as labelled. It then found 20 places: 16 were real and are converted with `.ToLocalTime()`; the rest already say UTC.
- Real ones, all five hours off on this workstation: specimen expiry on the test worklist, the result entry panel, the chart's Tests tab, and the four issue-desk boards; crossmatch expiry on Ready to issue, Retrospective, In transit, Issued units, and the chart's Products row and selected unit; ward receipt on Issued units; CBER and written-report recorded times on Reactions; alert acknowledged and cleared times; deviation closed date.

A specimen or crossmatch expiry shown in UTC as if local reads hours later than it is here: a crossmatch could look valid when it has expired. Issue is judged on the stored time and was never affected; the display now matches it.

- Guard: failed on the 20 places, passes after; full web suite passes.
- Live (read-only): the Alerts page heads "Raised"; a near-expiry alert cleared at 14:50 UTC (stored) now reads "Condition cleared 2026-11-08 09:50" in New York time, matching its Raised column (14:52 UTC, 09:52 local); before, it read 14:50. The development data had no in-date crossmatch or specimen expiry on a worklist row to compare. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-697, FRS-BB-814.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-812.

### Next

- Group same-kind alerts raised together (reagent QC by lot, near expiry by unit) into one row with acknowledge-all.

## Iteration 656 — Alerts of one kind raised together are one row (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (operations: alerts inbox)

The development inbox had 20 open alerts and about six things to do: seven "Reagent QC overdue: lot …" raised by one scan, eight "Near expiry: W…" raised by another, one massive transfusion protocol still open, a transfusion not completed, two units-expired sweeps, and a stock shortage. The protocol and the unfinished transfusion sat among fifteen near-identical rows, each acknowledged one at a time.

### Design

- `AlertInboxView.Rows`: three or more open alerts with the same source and severity whose titles share the text before ": ", raised within five minutes of each other, are one row: the shared heading with a count, each item (lot, unit) linked to its own target, the earliest raised time, one note, **Acknowledge all (n)**, and **Show each** to list them. The row sits where its first alert was, so most severe first still holds.
- Critical alerts are never grouped; two of a kind, or the same kind raised hours apart, stay separate.
- Acknowledge all acknowledges each alert through the existing call with the shared note, so each is recorded with the user and note as before; if one fails, the page says how many were acknowledged and names the rest.

### Verification

- Unit: grouping of three lots raised together; a fourth lot raised hours later, two near-expiry alerts, and three critical excursions stay separate; order kept; items, link, raised time, severity.
- Rendered: the grouped row names and links each lot, Show each and Hide each, the lone alert stays; Acknowledge all reports success, and a failure names the alert not acknowledged.
- Live (read-only): the 20 open alerts read as 7 rows: the protocol still open, two units-expired sweeps, "Reagent QC overdue (7)", the transfusion not completed, the stock shortage, and "Near expiry (8)". Nothing acknowledged. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-698, FRS-BB-815.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-813, TEST-BB-814, TEST-BB-815.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix: interface retry/error management (the HL7 error queue) for remembered or retyped information.

## Iteration 657 — Specimen label designer (2026-11-10)

### Request

Add a specimen label designer in Administration so users can design custom specimen labels, including aliquot labels, placing the barcode and data elements on a canvas that represents the label.

### What existed

One specimen label layout, fixed at 2 × 1 in, on a three-panel designer shared with the P-tag (fields dragged onto a canvas, the specimen ID as a barcode, audited saves). Every specimen label printed on it. No other sizes, no second design, nothing for aliquots, and the canvas showed field captions in a fixed font rather than what would print.

### Design

- **Designs.** `SpecimenLabelDesign`: code, name, purpose (Tube or Aliquot), size in dots at 203 dpi, the layout, default, active, version. Several per purpose; one active default each. Created from size presets (2 × 1, 2.25 × 1.25, 3 × 1, 2 × 0.75, 1.5 × 0.5, 1 × 0.5 in) or a custom size (0.5–4 by 0.25–3 in), as a starter fitted to the size or a copy of another design. Make default moves the default; the default cannot be deactivated until another takes its place. Every change is audited with a configuration-history snapshot (admin.config.edit).
- **Rules** (`SpecimenLabelDesignRules`). Required: the specimen ID as a barcode, so the tube scans (a hard stop on save and in the designer). Refused: an empty design, blank static text, the aliquot number on a tube design. Warned: fewer than two patient identifiers (OCD-080, the laboratory's decision), an aliquot design without the aliquot number, a barcode estimated (Code 128, 12-character ID, its bar width) to run off the side or bottom.
- **Canvas** (`LabelCanvasEditor`, now shared with the P-tag designer, which keeps its behaviour). Elements are drawn at scale with sample data at printed size; a barcode as a box of its estimated printed width. The selected element's X/Y (dots), font or bar height, bold, barcode, bar width (1–4) and digits under the barcode; arrow keys nudge (Shift 10 dots), Delete removes. The design is re-checked as it changes, with Save disabled while it has errors. New elements: sex, collected by, and on aliquot designs "Aliquot n of N".
- **Printing.** A specimen label prints on the design named, or the default tube design, and the job records the design code; an aliquot design, or an unknown or inactive code, is refused rather than printed on another design. Aliquot labels: 1–50 on the named or default aliquot design, one audited job each, "Aliquot n of N", the barcode the parent specimen ID (no separate aliquot identifier exists; OCD-080 asks whether one is needed). A reprint uses the design the label was printed with. The Printing page offers the active designs and, for an aliquot design, the count.
- **Migration of what exists.** The seed adds, once, TUBE-STD from the layout already saved on the old designer (so labels print as before) and ALIQ-STD (1.5 × 0.5 in), both defaults. `/admin/specimen-label` redirects to `/admin/specimen-labels`. The 40-dot barcode floor is unchanged.

### Safety (question 6)

A label that cannot be scanned, or that identifies the wrong specimen, is a transfusion risk: the specimen ID barcode is required on every design, an aliquot carries its parent's ID, and printing on a design that does not exist or is inactive is refused rather than falling back to another layout. Whether two patient identifiers must be enforced is recorded as OCD-080 rather than invented.

### Verification

- Unit: rules (refusals, warnings, sizes, barcode width, starters fit, normalising).
- Integration: create, copy, refusals, audit and history; save checks, warnings, version; default and active; permission; printing on the default and a named design, refusals; aliquot labels one job each with the bar width and parent ID, bounds, reprint on the printed design; the seed once.
- Rendered: the list and its actions; a design on its canvas (scale, sample data, barcode width, aliquot element); keyboard nudge, X/Y bounds, Delete; the live check and Save; the Printing page's design and aliquot count.
- Live (nothing saved or printed): the seed added TUBE-STD (2 × 1 in, 7 elements, from the saved layout) and ALIQ-STD (1.5 × 0.5 in, 5 elements), both default; `/admin/specimen-label` redirects to the list. The aliquot design opens with sample data at 1.84× and no warnings; clicking "Collected by" adds and selects it; ArrowRight moves it 16→17 and Shift+ArrowDown 82→92; the canvas shows it overlapping the specimen ID text where it was placed. In a narrow window the designer stacks its columns. The P-tag designer on the shared canvas is unchanged (609 × 456, 12 fields, 14 palette entries). No server errors. Found and fixed while walking: sizes read "1.50 × 0.50" beside "2 × 1"; the canvas pushed the settings off a narrow card.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-699, URS-BB-700; FRS-BB-816, FRS-BB-817, FRS-BB-818; OCD-080.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-816 to TEST-BB-831.

### Next

- A test print from the designer (a sample label on a chosen printer without a real specimen).

## Iteration 658 — Test print from the label designer (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (administration: label design)

Cycle 657's designer showed a label at scale, but the only way to see one printed was the Printing page, with a real specimen and a print job recorded against that patient, and only after saving the design. A layout that looks right on screen can still be unscannable on a worn printhead or small stock.

- **Test print** under the canvas, for the layout as it stands (saved or not), rendered at the design's size: a PDF or the ZPL shown on the page, or sent to an active Zebra (scaled to its dpi) or PDF printer.

Refused: an unknown design, an inactive printer, two printers at once, a user without admin.config.edit. Unavailable while the design has errors.

### Safety (question 6)

A test label stuck on a tube by mistake would identify no patient and scan to no specimen; nothing about it can be mistaken for a real label.

## Iteration 659 — The label designer warns about overlaps (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (administration: label design)

Walking the designer in Cycle 657, an added "Collected by" sat on top of the specimen ID text. The canvas showed it, but nothing said so, and on a 0.5 in label two lines a few dots apart are easy to miss on screen and unreadable on the label.

- Warnings only: the estimate uses sample data, and real names vary. The built-in tube layout and the starters stay free of warnings.

- Live (nothing saved): ALIQ-STD opens with no overlaps and no warnings; adding "Collected by" (placed at y 82) outlines it and the specimen ID text in red and says "Specimen ID and Collected by overlap. Move one of them."; moving it to x 152 clears both. No server errors.

## Iteration 660 — Outbound messages that have not gone (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (interoperability: retry and error management)

The HL7 error queue was empty, but the message log held seven outbound DFT charges from Nov 3–6 still "Received", unacknowledged, each with a Send button. The sender polls every 15 seconds; with no enabled outbound interface (or with retries spent) a message waits forever, and since nothing errored it never reached the error queue, the home card, or the handoff. In production that is results the EHR never got or charges billing never saw, with no one told. "Received" was also the wrong word for something waiting to go out.

### Design

- `OutboundMessageWaitRule`: why a message waits (no enabled interface that can send; retries spent; last send failed, retried; queued) and stuck after 15 minutes.
- `Hl7OutboundSender.ListWaitingAsync` (`GET /api/hl7/outbound/waiting`): outbound messages Received or Errored, oldest first, with reason and stuck flag; a charge withheld because it was cancelled is excluded, as the sender skips it.
- HL7 page: **Waiting to send** card (reason, age marked when stuck, Send, View); the log reads **Queued** for an outbound message not yet sent.
- Home card **HL7 outbound not sent** (hl7.manage, Supervisor desk): count stuck, note the oldest and how many wait for an interface or have spent retries; always under Needs attention when non-zero.

### Verification

- Integration: without an interface, queued and failed messages wait for one, oldest first, stuck past 15 minutes; acknowledged, inbound and withheld messages excluded; with an interface each reason is right; a disabled interface counts as none.
- Unit: the card's permission, desk and note.
- Rendered: the waiting card with reasons and the stuck mark; Queued in the log for outbound, Received for inbound.
- Live (read-only; nothing sent): the HL7 page shows "Waiting to send (7)", the seven DFT charges aged 3–7 days, each "No enabled outbound interface is set up to send it."; the log reads Queued for all seven; the home screen shows "HL7 outbound not sent 7 · oldest 7 d; 7 with no interface set up" under Needs attention. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-703, FRS-BB-821.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-837 to TEST-BB-840.

### Next

- Count stuck outbound messages on the shift handoff, as the error queue is.

The service counts from the message log (the application layer does not reach the HL7 sender); the reasons stay on the HL7 page.
- Handoff item "HL7 outbound not sent" linked to the HL7 page; summary "HL7 outbound not sent N".

## Iteration 662 — Recorded outages for downtime recovery (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (interoperability: downtime workflows)

Downtime has a patient summary to print before an outage, a reconciliation snapshot after it, and back-entry of paper issues. Nothing recorded the outage itself. After recovery, the person back-entering had to remember when the system was down, retype the same reason on every paper issue, and nothing questioned a paper time that fell outside the outage (a mistyped date). Question 2 (what must the user remember?) and question 3 (can the application infer it?) both pointed here.

### Design

- **`DowntimeEpisode`**: start, end (null while open), what was down, recorded and ended by. Never deleted; ending is its own audited action. Migration `20261225000000_DowntimeEpisodes`, dev bootstrap table, migrator order.
- **`DowntimeEpisodeRule`**: a description is required; no start or end in the future; the end after the start; no overlap, so only one outage is open at a time. `Covering` finds the outage a time falls in; `CheckPaperTime` warns outside every outage, and stays silent when none is recorded; `BackEntryReason` is "Issued on paper during downtime #n: description".
- **`DowntimeEpisodeService`**: list (newest 20, each with the paper back-entries whose issue time falls inside and those still Issued), record and end (issue.downtime-backentry; audited). Endpoints under `/api/compliance/downtime-episodes`; reading needs issue.create.
- **Downtime Snapshot**: an Outages card. The open outage stands out with End outage (the time defaulting to now). The table shows the window, what was down, the back-entries (still-open ones linked to Issued units) and who recorded and ended it. Record an outage is open when none is recorded.
- **Issue desk back-entry**: shows the open or latest outage and fills the reason from it; a paper time inside another outage switches to that one (unless the reason was typed); outside every outage it warns to check the record. With none recorded, it links to record one.

### Safety (questions 6 and 7)

The outside-outage check is a warning, not a stop: whether a back-entry outside a recorded outage should be refused, or need an override, is a clinical and quality decision (OCD-081). Every issue check runs as before; the outage changes only the offered reason and the warning.

### Verification

- Unit: covering outage, open outage to now, the warning and its absence with no outage, the current outage offered, adjacent outages allowed, overlaps and long descriptions refused.
- Integration: record open, end, audited; ending again and an unknown outage refused; future start or end, end before start, overlap, a second open outage and an end across another outage refused with nothing saved; back-entries counted per outage (normal issues and those outside excluded; still Issued counted).
- Rendered: the downtime card (open outage, End outage with the time filled, the table, the record form enabling); back-entry filling the reason, switching outage by paper time, warning outside.
- Live (read-only; nothing recorded): the dev database took the table on start; Downtime Snapshot shows the Outages card with "No outage recorded" and the record form open; ticking back-entry on the Issue desk shows "No outage is recorded" linked to /downtime, the reason left blank. No server errors. The snapshot's "Generated" time was a local time labelled UTC; the label is removed.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-705, FRS-BB-823; OCD-081.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-843 to TEST-BB-848.

### Next

- Show an open outage on the home screen for issuing roles, and add it to the shift handoff, so an outage left open is not forgotten.

## Iteration 665 — A back-entry outside every outage needs a reason (OCD-081 decided) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (interoperability: downtime; safety: overrides)

OCD-081 was decided on 2026-11-10 (option B). Cycle 662 only warned, on the page, when a paper issue time fell outside every recorded outage; the server took the entry with nothing recorded about it.

### Design

- `DowntimeEpisodeRule.CheckPaperTime` now takes the reason: outside every recorded outage it is a hard stop (`DT-EPISODE-OUTSIDE`) until a reason is given (at most 500 characters). No outage recorded, or a time inside one, needs nothing (option D not chosen).
- `IssuingService` applies it to every back-entry; the reason is kept on the issue (`Issue.OutsideOutageReason`, migration `20261227000000_IssueOutsideOutageReason`, dev bootstrap column) and in the issue audit with the other back-entry facts. Nothing is issued while refused.
- The Issue desk's outside warning now carries a required reason field, sent with the issue.

### Safety (question 7)

The reason is the control the product owner chose: a time outside the recorded outage is either a misread paper record (caught by the warning) or an outage nobody recorded (explained and kept). Every other issue check runs as before.

### Verification

- Unit: blank reason stops, a reason passes, over-long refused, no outages passes.
- Integration: a back-entry outside the only recorded outage is refused with nothing issued; with a reason it is issued, the reason on the issue and in the audit; the existing back-entry tests (no outage list) are unchanged.
- Rendered: the outside warning shows the reason field.
- Live (read-only): the API added the Issues column on start and the Issue desk loads with back-entry offered. The dev data has no recorded outage, so the outside path was exercised by the tests only. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-708, FRS-BB-826; OCD-081 decided.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-854; TEST-BB-843 and TEST-BB-848 updated.

## Iteration 666 — An override to continue during a reaction investigation (OCD-078 decided) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (patient-product workflows; safety: overrides)

OCD-078 was decided on 2026-11-10 (option C). Issue and the Transfusion desk only warned on screen that a reaction was under investigation; another unit could be issued and started with nothing recorded about the decision to continue.

### Design

- `ReactionUnderInvestigationRule` (`ISS-REACTION-OPEN`): a warning when the patient's investigation is open or under review and was reported at or before the stated issue or start time. A unit issued or started earlier (a late entry or a start documented afterwards) is not asked about.
- Issue: the warning joins the issue gate, so the usual issue override applies (issue.override, reason, authorizer), recorded and sent to supervisor review.
- Bedside start and one-step documentation: `OverrideReason` and `AuthorizedBy` on the requests; missing either refuses (nothing recorded); both record an override (context the unit, rule `ISS-REACTION-OPEN`) and an Override audit naming the investigation and issue. No extra permission at the bedside: the authorizer is the physician who decided.
- Transfusion desk: the reason and authorizer fields sit under the warning, cleared for each unit.

### Safety (questions 6 and 7)

The decision to continue is the physician's; the system now records it each time, with who decided, and puts it in front of a supervisor.

### Verification

- Unit: warns after the report, not before or without an investigation.
- Integration: an issue after the report needs the override and records it; bedside start without the authorizer is refused with no transfusion; with both it starts, the override and audit recorded. TEST-BB-768 (a late entry before the report) still issues without one.
- Rendered: the Issue form and Transfusion desk wording; the desk shows the two fields.
- Live (read-only): Issued units loads; no unit in the dev data belongs to a patient with an open reaction, so the override path was exercised by the tests only. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-709, FRS-BB-827; OCD-078 decided.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-855, TEST-BB-856; TEST-BB-753 and TEST-BB-755 updated.

## Iteration 667 — Open-system and pooled thawed shelf lives (OCD-068 decided) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (blood products: thawing, expiration calculations)

OCD-068 was decided on 2026-11-10 (option C). A product thawed in place got its code's one thawed shelf life whatever happened to the bag, so a unit entered during thawing, or a pool, could carry the longer closed-system dating.

### Design

- `AutoThawProduct.OpenSystemShelfLifeHours` and `PooledShelfLifeHours`, null until the facility sets them, edited with the closed time on Admin › Auto thaw products (reason required, configuration history); the table says *Not set (thaw refused)*.
- The thaw prompt (chart and unit page) asks **Thawed in an open system**; a pool is inferred from the unit's pooling modification, not asked (question 3).
- `ThawedExpirationRule.ShelfLifeFor`: the closed time for a closed single unit, otherwise the open-system and/or pooled time, the shorter when both apply. A needed time that is not set refuses the thaw, never falling back to the longer closed time (question 6).
- The thaw records open system, pooled, and the hours applied (`AutoThawRequest`, migration `20261228000000_AutoThawOpenSystemAndPooled`, dev bootstrap columns) and in the audit.
- No hours shipped: the facility enters them from its SOP and the circular of information.

### Verification

- Unit: each combination, the minimum, refusals when not set, optional range.
- Integration: open-system thaw refused until set, then 4 hours applied and recorded; an out-of-range setting refused; a pooled unit refused until set, then the shorter time applied when also open.
- Live (read-only): the API added the new columns on start; Admin › Auto thaw products loads, but the dev data has no auto-thaw codes, so the new columns and the thaw checkbox were exercised by the tests only. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-710, FRS-BB-828; OCD-068 decided.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-857, TEST-BB-858.

- OCD-072 option B: a shipment to another facility records the container, packing temperature, packer and receiving contact.

## Iteration 669 — Outside antibody reports documented and confirmed here (OCD-073 decided) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (antibody history; safety)

OCD-073 was decided on 2026-11-10 (option C). An antibody reported by another facility was recorded with the facility and date, and counted for selection, but nothing said how the report reached the bank, and nothing distinguished one this laboratory had confirmed from one taken on report.

### Design

- `AntibodyHistory.ReportKind` (a copy kept, a phone report), `ReportDocumentation`, `ConfirmedUtc`, `ConfirmedBy`, `ConfirmationNote` (migration `20261230000000_OutsideAntibodyConfirmation`, dev bootstrap).
- Recording an outside report requires how it is documented and the detail (what copy and where; who called). The user recording it is who took a phone report.
- It still counts for selection at once (the safer side). Every antibody warning (chart header, issue desk, test worklist, reaction investigation) says "not yet confirmed here" or "confirmed here".
- **Confirm** on the chart row (immuno.record) records the testing here that confirmed it; audited; refused for a local antibody, a blank note, an inactive record, or twice.
- Older outside reports read "Report not documented" and unconfirmed.

### Safety (question 6)

Nothing about selection changes: an unconfirmed outside antibody still drives antigen-negative selection. What changes is that everyone sees it has not been confirmed, and the report behind it is on record.

### Verification

- Unit: documentation required only with a facility, after the facility and date checks; confirm refusals; wording.
- Integration: refusals add nothing; recorded with documentation and unconfirmed; confirmed with note and audit; second confirm refused.
- Rendered: documentation, unconfirmed badge, Confirm with its note, confirmed line, documentation fields on Add antibody.
- Live (read-only; nothing saved): the API added the columns on start; on a chart, typing a reporting facility under Add antibody shows "Documented by" (a copy kept, a phone report) and the detail field. No demo patient has an outside report (seeding one would change selection for a demo patient), so the badge and Confirm were exercised by the rendered and integration tests. No server errors.

- URS-BB-712, FRS-BB-830; OCD-073 decided (the confirmation list is next).

## Iteration 670 — Outside antibody reports to confirm (OCD-073 completed) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (operations: worklists; antibody history)

Cycle 669 marked outside reports "not yet confirmed here" on each chart, but nothing gathered them: confirming one depended on someone opening that chart. OCD-073 option C asked for a confirmation task.

### Design

- `ListOutsideToConfirmAsync` (`GET /api/antibodies/outside-to-confirm`, immuno.record): active outside reports with no confirmation, oldest first, merged-away charts left out, each with the patient and whether the report was documented.
- Antibody ID: **Outside reports to confirm** below the open workups, each row opening the chart where **Confirm** is.
- Home card **Outside antibodies to confirm** (immuno.record; Bench and Supervisor desks): the count, the oldest wait, and how many have no documented report. Not urgent: the antibody already counts for selection (question 6).

### Verification

- Unit: the card's permission, desks, link and note.
- Integration: only active, unconfirmed outside reports listed, oldest first, documentation flagged; confirmed, inactive and local antibodies left out.
- Rendered: the worklist section with the facility and date, the undocumented note, and the chart link.
- Live (read-only): Antibody ID shows "Outside reports to confirm (0)" with its empty message, and the home card "Outside antibodies to confirm" is listed under Clear, linked to the section; the dev data has no outside report. No server errors.

## Iteration 671 — RhIG suggested candidacy and calculated dose (OCD-069 decided) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (antibody/antigen history: RhIG)

OCD-069 was decided on 2026-11-10 (option C). The RhIG evaluation listed the facts and left both the candidacy and the vial count to be worked out by hand from the procedure, every time.

### Design

- `RhigDoseRule.Suggest`: Rh positive or an Rh-negative infant suggests not a candidate; Rh negative with no anti-D and an infant Rh positive or not known suggests a candidate; no Rh type on file, or anti-D on history (passive or immune is the reviewer's call), suggests nothing. Weak D and partial D are not recorded in the patient's Rh type, so they are not treated (left to the medical director).
- `RhigDoseRule.Calculate`: % fetal cells × maternal blood volume ÷ mL per vial, rounded up, to the nearest plus one, or up plus one; the working is shown. Facility Policies *RhIG dose* settings (mL per vial, maternal blood volume, rounding) ship 0: nothing is calculated, and the evaluation says why.
- The reviewer confirms: **Use the suggestion** fills the decision and vials for the reviewer to save. Completion keeps the suggestion and the calculated vials on the record (migration `20261231000000_RhigSuggestionAndDose`, dev bootstrap), audited, so later setting changes do not rewrite it; a recorded dose or decision differing from them is marked.

### Safety (question 6)

Nothing is decided by the application: the decision and vials are still what the reviewer records, and completion still needs result verification. The calculation only appears once the medical director has entered the settings.

### Verification

- Unit: each rounding, the minimum of one vial when rounding up, nothing without quantitation or settings, the explanation; each suggestion case.
- Integration: open evaluation suggests without a dose until set; with settings, 3 vials and the working; completion stores and audits them; a later rounding change leaves the completed record's values.
- Rendered: suggestion and working on an open evaluation, the completed record's line and differs badge, Use the suggestion filling the vials.
- Live (read-only): the demo open evaluation (MRN0026) reads "Suggested candidate: the patient is Rh negative with no anti-D, and the infant is Rh positive" with no dose (no quantitation); Facility Policies lists the three RhIG dose settings at 0. Demo evaluations completed before this change read "No suggestion or calculated dose was kept when this evaluation was completed" (first shown as "none", which read as a finding; reworded). No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-714, FRS-BB-832; OCD-069 decided (settings and weak/partial D policy remain with the medical director).

### Tests

- TEST-BB-868, TEST-BB-869, TEST-BB-870.

### Next

- OCD-074 option B: neonatal pretransfusion testing (one specimen per admission, no repeat ABO/Rh, no crossmatch with a negative screen) from facility settings, shipped off.

## Iteration 672 — An infant's specimen valid for the admission (OCD-074, part one) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (orders and specimens: specimen expiration)

OCD-074 was decided on 2026-11-10 (option B): for infants under four months, one specimen covers the admission, ABO/Rh is not repeated, and no crossmatch is needed when the antibody screen is negative, enforced from facility settings. Specimens for infants expired like everyone else's, so a neonate needed a new tube every three days. The three parts touch different checks, so they are built one at a time; this is the first.

### Design

- Facility Policies *Neonatal pretransfusion testing rules* (`Neonatal.RulesEnabled`, off) and *Neonatal age limit (days)* (`Neonatal.AgeLimitDays`, 120). Off by default until the medical director confirms the rules against the current AABB Standards.
- `NeonatalTestingRule`: an infant younger than the limit at collection, on a visit not yet discharged, gets a specimen valid until discharge or the age limit, whichever is first, never earlier than its usual expiration. Not applied with explicit validity hours or without a visit.
- The usual expiration is kept (`Specimen.NeonatalStandardExpiresUtc`, migration `20270101000000_NeonatalAdmissionSpecimen`, dev bootstrap) so discharge (on the chart or by ADT) ends the specimen at discharge but not before the usual time, audited. The alloimmunization recompute leaves these specimens alone.
- The chart's Expires column says *For the admission (infant)*.

### Safety (question 6)

Off until the medical director turns it on. Any infant specimen extended stays tied to its visit and ends at discharge or the age limit; past the limit the usual rules apply.

### Verification

- Unit: under the limit until the day it is reached; dating to discharge or the limit, never below the usual; nothing without the rules, a visit, or an open visit; discharge.
- Integration: off keeps the usual expiration; on extends to the age limit with the usual kept and audited; an infant past the limit keeps the usual; discharge ends it at discharge, audited; another specimen is unchanged.
- Live (read-only; the rules left off): the API added the Specimens column on start; Facility Policies lists *Neonatal pretransfusion testing rules* (false) and *Neonatal age limit (days)* (120); a chart's Specimens tab loads. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-715, FRS-BB-833; OCD-074 part one.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-871, TEST-BB-872.

### Next

- OCD-074 part two: no repeat ABO/Rh during the admission (the second determination for an infant under the neonatal rules).

## Iteration 673 — An infant's ABO/Rh not repeated during the admission (OCD-074, part two) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (safety rules: duplicate testing; patient-product workflows)

Part two of OCD-074 option B. With part one an infant's specimen covered the admission, but routine red-cell issue still demanded a second concordant ABO/Rh from a separate specimen, so the infant needed a second tube anyway: the neonatal rules said not to repeat ABO/Rh.

### Design

- `NeonatalTestingRule.AdmissionTypeStands`: the infant's current type was tested on an admission specimen (one made valid for the admission under the neonatal rules, Cycle 672) that is still valid. The specimen already records that the rules applied when it was collected, so the server and the chart decide the same way without another setting lookup.
- Where it counts: the cellular issue check (`ISS-SECOND-ABO`), the Second ABO/Rh desk (the infant is not listed), Ready to issue (not flagged), and the chart header ("Infant: stands for the admission", no missing-second-type notice).
- Where it does not: electronic crossmatch still needs two determinations; after discharge or the age limit the specimen expires and the usual rule returns.

### Safety (question 6)

Off unless the facility has turned on the neonatal rules (part one); tied to a specimen of this admission, still valid, so it cannot carry over to a later visit. Electronic crossmatch is left strict.

### Verification

- Unit: stands only on an admission specimen still valid.
- Integration: the infant is issued red cells with one type from the admission specimen and is off the Second ABO/Rh desk; the same type on an ordinary specimen is still refused and listed.
- Rendered: header note in place of the notice; the notice returns on an ordinary or expired specimen.
- Live (read-only; neonatal rules off in dev): the Second ABO/Rh desk lists its one patient as before and a chart header loads. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-716, FRS-BB-834; OCD-074 part two.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-873, TEST-BB-874, TEST-BB-875.

### Next

- OCD-074 part three: no crossmatch for an infant when the antibody screen is negative.

## Iteration 674 — Infant group O red cells without a crossmatch (OCD-074, part three) (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (safety rules: crossmatch; patient-product workflows)

The last part of OCD-074 option B: no crossmatch for an infant when the antibody screen is negative. Issue still demanded a compatible crossmatch for every red-cell unit to an infant.

### Design

- `NeonatalTestingRule.NoCrossmatchApplies`: the infant's type stands for the admission (part two), a current verified negative screen with no positive screen and no antibody history, red cells or whole blood, **group O**, routine issue (not emergency or MTP, which keep their own path).

Off unless the neonatal rules are on; tied to the admission specimen; group O only; any antibody, positive screen, or emergency path keeps the crossmatch requirement. A new open decision (OCD-082) records what was not decided.

- Integration: group O to an infant with a negative screen issued without a crossmatch and marked in the issue and audit; group A to the same kind of infant refused; an infant on an ordinary specimen refused.

- New page `/inventory/return-to-supplier/list?key=`: the reason, returned when and by whom, the suppliers, each unit with a receiver-initials column, and a Handed over block (courier or supplier, date/time, container and temperature, signature). Unknown or missing key: no sheet and no Print.
- Read-only.
- Demo: two group A red cells returned yesterday for "Supplier recall R-DEMO-01" (W000123RTS0001, W000123RTS0002), each with its status row, added once, so the list has something to show.

## Iteration 687 — A recall does not stop at a component it cannot recall (2026-11-10)

### Capability matrix rescan (patient-product workflows: recall and lookback; safety)

While looking at returns after Cycle 686: a recall by DIN tried to recall every component not transfused or shipped. A component already returned to the supplier, a modified parent unit, or an expired unit cannot become Recalled (the status rules allow nothing after ReturnedToSupplier or Modified, and only discard or quarantine after Expired). The recall then failed with "Could not recall unit …", after the components earlier in the list had already been saved as Recalled: a part-done recall, and the components after it still on the shelf for issue. Question 6: this could leave a recalled donation's components available.

### Design

- `LookbackRecallRule.WhyNotRecalled(status)` uses the status rules, not a new list: a component whose move to Recalled is not allowed is left as it is, with why (returned to the supplier; modified into the units listed under the donation; expired, so discard it; otherwise its status). Transfused, shipped, already recalled and discarded are handled as before.
- `RecallByDinAsync` checks it after the recipient-notification step (an issued or transfused component still opens its notification), recalls the rest, and records the components left in the recall audit.
- The report carries them (`NotRecalled`); Lookback shows a warning naming each, linked to its unit.
- No status rule changed, and no unit's status is overwritten.

### Verification

- Unit: each status named or not.
- Integration: a donation with a unit on the shelf, one returned to the supplier and one expired: the recall succeeds, the shelf unit is Recalled, the other two keep their status and are named with why. Before the change this recall failed.
- Rendered: after a recall, the note names the component with why and links to it.
- Live (read-only): a recall writes, so it was not run on the dev data; the Lookback page loads with Recall all components and no note before a recall. The recall path is covered by the integration and rendered tests. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-730, FRS-BB-848.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-911, TEST-BB-912, TEST-BB-913.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 688 — Recalled units to pull (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (operations: worklists; recall)

After Cycle 687 a recall reaches every component it can. A recalled unit then sits in Recalled status (it cannot be issued) until someone finds it and quarantines or discards it (a return to the supplier goes through quarantine), but nothing listed those units: no board, no home card. Only a status search on Inventory found them. Question 5: the next step after a recall was not surfaced. Question 6: a recalled unit that was issued (a recall moves Issued to Recalled) is on the ward and has to be brought back.

### Design

- `InventoryService.ListRecalledAsync`: units in Recalled status, oldest recall first, each with the recall's reason, time and who, and what the unit was before (from the status row the recall wrote). `GET /api/inventory/units/recalled`.
- Inventory board **Recalled** (`board=recalled`): unit, ABO/Rh, product, location, recall reason, recalled when and by whom, expiry, Open. A unit that was issued is marked *Was issued: on the ward*. The board button shows the count.
- Home card **Recalled units to pull** (inventory.discard or inventory.release; Issue desk and Supervisor desk): urgent above zero, ordered before Expired on shelf.
- Read-only: the disposition stays on the unit page (quarantine or discard; the status rules send a return to the supplier through quarantine), with its existing checks and audit.

### Verification

- Unit: who sees the card, its link and desks, and its order before Expired on shelf.
- Integration: a recalled shelf unit and a recalled issued unit are listed with reason, time, who and what they were; a unit never recalled is not; a quarantined one leaves the list.
- Rendered: the board from the card's link with both rows and the on-ward mark; the empty board says so.
- Live (read-only): the dev data has no recalled units; the home page shows the Recalled units to pull card, and Inventory opened from it shows the Recalled board, empty, with its guidance. The guidance first said to return a recalled unit from its unit page, which the status rules do not allow (Recalled goes to quarantine or discard); it now says a return goes through quarantine. No server errors.

## Iteration 691 — A unit recalled while it is out (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (patient-product workflows: return, transfusion; safety)

A recall moves an issued unit to Recalled (the status rules allow Issued to Recalled). Following that unit:

- **Return:** the return path writes its status steps without the transition check and chooses Available when the inspection and time out of storage pass. A recalled unit brought back unused therefore went Recalled, Returned, Available: back in stock for the next patient, with the recall left only in its recorded reason. Question 6: a recalled unit could be issued again.
- **Bedside:** starting its transfusion was refused, but as "This issue already has a transfusion record", which does not tell the nurse why or what to do.
- **Issued units:** nothing marked it.

### Design

- `ReturnUnitAsync`: a Recalled unit asked back to Available is refused ("returns to quarantine, not to stock"); otherwise `ReturnRecalledAsync` closes the issue as returned, records the Return (not reissue eligible), and moves the unit from Recalled straight to quarantine coded **Lookback recall**, "Returned after recall (<recall reason>): <return reason>", audited. No inspection can change that.
- `StartTransfusionAsync`: a Recalled unit is refused with `ComponentRecalled`, the recall reason, and "Do not transfuse it; return it to the blood bank."
- `ListOutstandingIssuedAsync` marks `UnitRecalled` with the reason; Issued units shows **Recalled: do not transfuse, return it**.
- No status rule changed; the path no longer writes a step the rules do not allow (Recalled goes to Quarantine, which they do).

### Verification

- Integration: an issued, received unit recalled: the start is refused naming the recall and no transfusion is recorded; the issued row is marked with the reason; a return to Available is refused; a return with every inspection passed ends in Quarantine coded Lookback recall with the note, the issue Returned, the last status step Recalled to Quarantine, an audit entry, and the row off the issued list.
- Rendered: the recalled unit's badge with the reason; the other unit has none.
- Live (read-only): Issue & Transfuse lists the 10 demo issued units with no recalled badge (none of them is recalled); the list loads with the new recall lookup. The recall-while-issued path is covered by the tests. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-734, FRS-BB-852.

- TEST-BB-922, TEST-BB-923.

The board's scan refuses the unit recalled while issued and leaves it Recalled.

## Iteration 694 — Issuing status steps follow the status rules (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (patient-product workflows: return; safety architecture)

Cycles 691 to 693 each found a unit that a return sent to Available from a status that should have kept it out of stock (Recalled, then Quarantine). The cause is shared: the issuing paths write their own status steps (`AppendStatus`) without the status rules every inventory action checks. Two more statuses the rules allow from Issued had the same outcome. A unit reported **Damaged** or **Missing** while out, then returned with a passing inspection, went Returned, then Available.

### Design

- `ReturnUnitAsync`:
  - **Damaged:** the unit refuses Available and stays Damaged, so the damage inspection on the Discrepancy board still applies. The issue is closed as returned.
  - **Missing:** the unit refuses Available. It is back, so it is quarantined as *Located after missing* pending inspection, as Locate does, and the missing reason is cleared.
  - **Recorded:** both are audited (Path ReturnReported), and neither return is reissue eligible.
  - **Other statuses:** any status other than Issued or ReturnPending (after the Recalled and Quarantine paths) is refused, naming it.
- `AppendStatus` checks `InventoryStatusTransition.IsAllowed` and throws when a step is not allowed. A future gap stops the action with a message naming the unit and the step, instead of leaving the unit in a status it should not reach. The full suite ran with the check in place before the new tests, with no failure, so no existing path relies on a disallowed step.

### Verification

- Integration: for a unit damaged, missing or expired while issued and received:
  - a return to Available is refused;
  - with every inspection passed, the damaged unit stays Damaged with its reason and the issue is returned;
  - the missing unit is in quarantine as located after missing, with its reason folded into the note;
  - the expired unit's return is refused and its issue stays open.
- Live (read-only; nothing returned): Issue & Transfuse opened on Issued units (desk=issued) lists the 10 demo units with Return offered. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-737, FRS-BB-855.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-928.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 695 — An EHR transfusion for a unit no longer issued (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (interoperability: BPAM inbound; safety architecture)

Following Cycle 694, every direct status write in the application was checked against the status rules:

- **Checked already:** allocation, release, discard, the expiry sweep, retype, the storage-excursion quarantine and modification.
- **Own allowed list:** the reaction remainder hold.
- **Not checked:** the inbound transfusion message (BPAM) from the EHR. If the EHR reported a unit transfused that the blood bank had since recalled, quarantined, or recorded as damaged or missing, it was moved to Transfused without a word. A recalled unit transfused that way left no sign beyond its status.

### Decision needed (OCD-083)

How such a transfusion should be recorded is a clinical decision, not invented here. OCD-083 offers four ways:

- **A:** record it, unit Transfused.
- **B:** record the event, keep the status, flag it.
- **C:** a supervisor documents it from the error queue.
- **D:** refuse it, and document it within the recall or investigation.

Until then the safe, reversible behavior is to hold the message.

### Design

- `InterfaceTransfusionService`: a unit not Issued or TransfusionStarted is refused, saying its status, the recall reason if recalled, "held for review and not recorded (OCD-083)". The HL7 processor turns that into a mapping error, so the message is in the error queue for review and replay. Nothing is recorded, and the unit and issue keep their status.
- Its own status writer refuses a step the rules do not allow, as the issuing paths do since Cycle 694.

### Verification

- Integration: for a unit recalled, quarantined or damaged after issue, the message fails with the status (and the recall), and no transfusion is recorded; unit and issue are unchanged. For a unit still issued, the same message records the transfusion and sets Transfused as before.
- The existing authorization test counted all transfusion events in its shared database; it now compares before and after.
- Live (read-only; no message sent): the API and the HL7 Interface page load as before. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-738, FRS-BB-856; OCD-083 opened.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-929.

### Next

- OCD-083 needs an answer before the held messages can be recorded.

It did not show why the unit was recalled, held or quarantined, though each reason is recorded on the unit. During a recall (Cycles 687-695) the first thing a technologist asks of a scanned unit is which recall, and that meant opening the unit page.

## Iteration 697 — The issue gate says what to do with a unit it will not issue (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (safety rules: issue gate; UX: human-readable errors)

Continuing the status audit of Cycles 694-695, I checked whether the issue gate could issue a unit in a status the rules do not allow (discarded, modified into other units, expected, expired), even as an emergency release. It cannot: the gate's unit-status rule refuses all of them, and the new test confirms it. The refusal itself was "Unit status Modified is not issuable.", which tells the issuer neither why nor what to do.

### Design

- `IssueGate.NotIssuableMessage(status)` keeps the sentence's start, so anything matching it still matches, and adds the reason and the next step per status:
  - not received yet: receive it first;
  - received but not released: release it (and retype it if required) first;
  - discarded: choose another unit;
  - modified into other units: issue one of those instead;
  - expired: discard it and choose another unit;
  - recalled: choose another unit;
  - in quarantine: choose another unit, or release it from quarantine first;
  - on operational hold: release the hold first, or choose another unit;
  - missing or damaged: resolve it on the Discrepancy board;
  - already issued or transfused;
  - left this facility.
- Other statuses end at the status. No rule changed.

### Verification

- Unit: each status's wording and the plain ending for the rest.
- Integration: discarded, modified, expected and expired units are refused as an emergency release with that wording; no issue is recorded and the status is unchanged (this confirms the existing gate).
- Live: not run; seeing the refusal would mean attempting an issue on the dev data, and only the wording changed, which the tests cover.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-740, FRS-BB-858.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-932, TEST-BB-933.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 700 — A reported transfusion recorded and reviewed (OCD-083 decided) (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (interoperability: BPAM inbound; supervisor queue)

OCD-083 was decided on 2026-11-11: option B. A transfusion the EHR reports for a unit that the blood bank had recalled, quarantined, or recorded as damaged or missing after it was issued is recorded (it happened, and lookback and the patient's record need it). The unit keeps that status, and the transfusion is flagged for review. Cycle 695 had held these messages in the error queue.

### Design

- `InterfaceTransfusionService` records the transfusion as usual and sets the issue Transfused, but:
  - the event keeps the unit's status (`TransfusionEvent.UnitStatusAtReport`);
  - the unit keeps its status and is marked `TransfusionReportedUtc`;
  - it is audited (Path TransfusedOverStatus);
  - the acknowledgment says the unit's status and that it is flagged for review;
  - a suspected reaction still opens an investigation, and billing is captured as for any transfusion.
- Any other status that is not issued (discarded, expired, returned...) is still held in the error queue.
- `TransfusionReportReviewService`: the unreviewed ones, and a review recorded once:
  - a note is required;
  - it needs inventory.release or override.approve;
  - the reviewer and time are recorded and audited;
  - unit and issue are not changed.
  `POST /api/transfusions/{id}/report-review`.
- Supervisor queue: kind **Reported transfusion**, before override review. The row names the unit, the patient's MRN, when, and the status with its reason. It offers Open unit and an in-place Review (note, Reviewed).
- The Recalled board, its home card and the handoff no longer count such a unit as one to pull, and the board's scan refuses it. The unit page says it was reported transfused, and when.
- Migration `20270106000000_TransfusionReportedOverStatus`, dev bootstrap columns.

### Verification

- Integration:
  - Recalled, quarantined, damaged and missing units are recorded with the status kept on the unit and the event, the issue transfused, the unit marked and the audit written. An issued unit is recorded as before, and a discarded unit is still refused.
  - On the queue, the reported transfusion is listed with the recall reason. A review without permission or without a note is refused; a review is recorded and audited and cannot be repeated; the row leaves the queue.
  - Such a recalled unit leaves the Recalled board and its scan is refused.
- Rendered: review in place on the supervisor queue; Reviewed waits for a note; the row leaves.
- Domain: the supervisor-queue kind count test now expects six kinds and checks the new kind is linkable.
- Live (read-only; no message sent): the API added the new columns and the supervisor queue reads them; the queue loads its 6 demo items with no reported transfusion; the Recalled board still shows the demo unit (not reported transfused). No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-743, FRS-BB-861; OCD-083 decided.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-929 (changed), TEST-BB-937, TEST-BB-938, TEST-BB-939, TEST-BB-940.
