- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 701 — A reported transfusion reads so on the patient's record (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (timeline views; supervisor queues)

Cycle 700 records a transfusion the EHR reported over a unit's status and puts it on the supervisor queue. The patient's own record did not say so: Product History and the timeline showed an ordinary transfusion. The home Supervisor queue card did not name these items, so they did not bring the card under Needs attention.

### Design

- `TransfusionReportNote.For(status, reviewedBy, note)`: "Reported by the EHR while the unit was <status> in the blood bank; review pending on the supervisor queue", or "...; reviewed by <who>: <what was found>".
- Product History: the transfusion row carries it as an entry note.
- Timeline: the transfusion event's detail adds it, and the event is a warning until the review is done.
- `SupervisorNote`: "n reported transfusion(s) to review".
- Read-only.

### Verification

- Unit: the note for no report, pending, reviewed with and without a note; the supervisor card note.
- Integration: the timeline event is a warning with the pending note, then Info with the review; the reported transfusion's product history row carries the note.
- Live (read-only): MRN0001's timeline loads with no reported transfusion (the demo has none). No server errors. The new note itself is covered by the tests.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-744, FRS-BB-862.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-941, TEST-BB-942, TEST-BB-943, TEST-BB-944.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 702 — A recall reaches the recipient of a reported transfusion (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (recall and lookback; safety)

After OCD-083 option B (Cycle 700), a unit can be quarantined, damaged or missing in the blood bank and yet reported transfused by the EHR. A later recall of its donation chose whom to notify from the unit's status alone. Such a unit is neither issued nor transfused, so its recipient got no notification. The recall also moved it (quarantine allows it) to Recalled, as if it were on a shelf. Question 6: a patient who received a recalled donation would not be notified.

### Design

- `RecallByDinAsync` treats a unit with `TransfusionReportedUtc` as transfused:
  - it opens the recipient notification for the transfusion's issue and patient;
  - it does not recall the unit, which keeps its status;
  - the recall's audit counts it among the pending notifications.
- No status rule changed.

### Verification

- Integration: a quarantined unit reported transfused, then its donation recalled. The notification names the patient and issue. The unit is not listed as "not recalled" and keeps its Quarantine status. The old code chose by status alone, so it would have recalled the unit and notified no one.
- Live: not run; a recall writes, and the dev data has no reported transfusion. Covered by the integration test.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-745, FRS-BB-863.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-945.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 703 — A reported-transfused unit keeps its status (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (blood products: status history; safety)

Following OCD-083 option B (Cycle 700) through inventory: a unit reported transfused while quarantined, damaged or missing kept that status and stayed on the Quarantine or Discrepancy board, and in the supervisor queue's items for them. Releasing it from quarantine or locating it would have made a unit already in a patient Available again. Inspecting or discarding it, or the expiry sweep, would change a status option B keeps. Question 6: phantom stock that could be selected.

### Design

- `ReportedTransfusionRule` (INV-REPORTED-TRANSFUSED): a unit with `TransfusionReportedUtc` keeps its status.
- `InventoryService.ChangeStatusAsync` hard-stops any change to another status, which covers release, locate, inspect, quarantine and recall. `DiscardAsync` hard-stops too, and the expiry sweep skips the unit.
- `ListQuarantineAsync` and `ListDiscrepancyAsync` leave it out, and with them the supervisor queue's quarantine-release and missing/damaged items. It is reviewed there as a reported transfusion instead (Cycle 700).
- No status rule changed.

### Verification

- Unit: the rule passes an ordinary unit and stops a reported one.
- Integration:
  - a quarantined unit reported transfused: release and discard are refused with the rule, and it is off the Quarantine board while another quarantined unit is on it;
  - a missing one: locate is refused, and it is off the Discrepancy board;
  - both keep their status.
- Live (read-only): the Quarantine board still lists the 3 demo quarantined units and the Discrepancy board the 2 missing or damaged ones (none is reported transfused). No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-746, FRS-BB-864.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-946, TEST-BB-947.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 705 — Import and download antigrams (user request) (2026-11-11)

### Request

"Add the ability for the user to import/manually add/download antibody antigrams from manufacturers." Asked and answered:

- **Download:** staff download the antigram from the manufacturer's site themselves and import it here, and the system exports antigrams. It does not fetch from vendor sites: they sit behind customer logins, and no vendor interface is documented here.
- **Formats:** CSV and Excel in one documented layout.

### Capability matrix rescan (testing: antibody identification; administration: panel lots)

Admin › Antibody panel lots already let a lot's antigram be entered by hand (New lot: cells, each typed for the catalog antigens). There was no import of a file and no download.

### Design

- `AntigramImport` (Domain) reads the layout:
  - **Header:** a header row whose first cell is "Cell" (title rows above skipped) and an optional Role column.
  - **Antigen columns:** matched to the catalog by exact code first (C and c kept apart), otherwise by a spelling that only one antigen fits (Fy(a), anti-Jka). A one-letter code of the other case never matches.
  - **Values:** + 0 w +het +hom, or blank for not tested; a leading apostrophe is ignored.
  - **Stops:** an unreadable value, a repeated cell, an unknown role, no header, no antigen column, or over 60 cells stops the import, so a slip never becomes "not tested". Unknown columns are listed and left out.
  - **Export:** `Header` and `Row` write the same layout, so an export reads back.
- `CsvFormat.ReadRows` and `SplitLine`: the CSV reader moved out of the interface translation import and shared by both.
- `SpreadsheetRows.ReadXlsx` (Web, ClosedXML at the Printing project's version) reads the first worksheet as text.
- New lot form: **Import an antigram** (CSV, TSV or XLSX up to 2 MB).
  - The cells in the form are replaced, and a summary says what was read and left out; a file with problems is not used and each problem is listed by line.
  - Nothing is saved until Create, with its existing checks.
  - The request carries the file name, and the lot's audit entry names it.
- **Download blank template** (every active antigen) in the form, and **Download antigram (CSV)** on a lot, with columns in catalog order.

### Verification

- Unit (parser):
  - a manufacturer-style sheet with title rows, roles, a loose antigen spelling, every value form, an autocontrol row and an extra column;
  - each problem that stops the import, and k never matching K;
  - an export reading back as the same cells.
- Rendered:
  - a CSV fills the cells and reports the left-out column;
  - a bad file is not used and the cells stay;
  - an Excel file fills the cells;
  - the template opens as a download;
  - a lot's antigram downloads in catalog order with the expected rows.
- Integration: an imported lot's audit names the file; a hand-entered one does not.
- Live (nothing saved): on Admin › Antibody panel lots, New lot, importing a CSV with a title row, K, E, C, c, Fy(a), JKA and a Donor column filled cells 1 to 3 and reported "3 cells and 6 antigens imported … Columns not in the antigen catalog were left out: Donor."; the form was left without creating a lot. A demo lot's Download antigram (CSV) gave "Cell,Role,K,E,C,c,FYA,JKA,JKB,M,N" and one row per cell. No server errors.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-748, FRS-BB-866.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-949 to TEST-BB-957.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 706 — Correct an antigram before the lot is used (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (testing: antibody identification; administration: panel lots)

After Cycle 705 a lot's antigram could be entered, imported and downloaded, and the help said to correct it before the bench uses the lot. Nothing could correct it: a mistyped cell or a manufacturer's corrected sheet meant deactivating the lot, and its lot number could not be used again.

### Design

- **When:** only while no workup (open, completed or voided) is linked to the lot. A workup's reactions were read against the cells as they stood, so once one exists the correction is refused (ABID-LOT-CORRECT-INUSE) and the page says to withdraw the lot, create a corrected one and review the workups.
- **Checks:** the edit permission, a reason (ABID-LOT-CORRECT-REASON), and the New lot cell checks (shared `AddCellStops`).
- **Nothing deleted:** the current cells get `SupersededUtc` and the corrected cells are added. The (LotId, CellNumber) unique index is filtered to current cells, so the same cell number can return. Every cell reader (the lot detail, the workup antigram, Assist, the autocontrol check, the reaction cell check, the demo seeder) leaves superseded cells out.
- **Audit:** the configuration change carries the cells before and after, the reason, and the file when imported.
- **UI:** **Correct antigram** on the lot (with no workups) opens the New lot cell editor filled with its cells, with the import and a reason; the identity fields are hidden. The expression list gains Weak, which an import could already produce.

### Verification

- Unit: the rule refuses a lot in use, a missing reason, and bad cells; passes a good correction.
- Integration: a correction supersedes the old cell, reuses its number, shows the new cells and audits before and after; a lot in use, no reason or no permission leaves the cells unchanged.
- Rendered: Correct antigram prefills the cells, needs a reason, and shows the corrected cells; a lot in use offers no correction and says why.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-749, FRS-BB-867.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-958 to TEST-BB-962.

### Next

- Back to the capability matrix.

## Iteration 707 — Panel lots to replace (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (testing: antibody identification; inventory of reagents)

Reagent lots warn before they expire (Reagent QC card, 7-day window). Antibody panel lots did not: the first sign that the last primary panel had expired was a workup refused at the bench (an inactive or expired lot is a hard stop), with no lot entered to take its place.

### Design

- `AntibodyPanelLotSupplyRule.Review`, per kind (primary panel, selected cells):
  - no active, unexpired lot: needs action (for selected cells only once a selected-cell lot has been entered);
  - a current lot expiring within `ReagentLotRule.ExpiringSoonDays` (7): listed, naming the later current lot of its kind that follows it; needs action only when none does.

- `GET /api/admin/antibody-panel-lots/supply` for admin.config.view or immuno.record.
- `PanelLotSupplyNotice` at the top of Admin › Antibody panel lots and of the Antibody ID worklist, with advice worded for who is reading.
- Home card **Panel lots to replace** (Bench and Supervisor desks) counting what needs action and naming the soonest; it opens the admin page, or the worklist for the bench.

### Verification

- Unit: expiring with and without a replacement, the window edge, inactive and expired lots ignored, wording for today and tomorrow; no current lot of a kind; the card's count, note, links and permissions.
- Integration: a created lot expiring in 2 days is listed with its days and message.
- Rendered: the panel lots page shows the notice.

- TEST-BB-963 to TEST-BB-967.

## Iteration 708 — Equipment register and scheduled checks (2026-11-11)

### Capability matrix rescan (operations: equipment)

Reagent lots, storage temperatures, and panel lots each have their checks, but bench equipment had none: no register of centrifuges, cell washers, heat blocks or irradiators, no record of their QC, calibration or maintenance, no list of what was due, and no way to mark one out of service. A modification recorded its device as free text.

### Design

- **Register:** `Equipment` (code as asset tag, unique, upper case; name, kind, location, serial), deactivated rather than deleted, and taken out of service with a reason (when, by whom), returned with a reason.
- **Checks:** `EquipmentCheck` per equipment: a name, an interval in days and the SOP instructions. The interval is the facility's; none is built in (the demo's are labelled examples).
- **Records:** `EquipmentCheckRecord`: performer (signed-in user), time, passed or failed, note; a failure needs a note.
- **Due:** `EquipmentCheckRule.Evaluate`: due its interval after the last pass, by date (a daily check done late yesterday is due today); never done is due now; a failed latest record stays Failed until a pass. Out-of-service equipment's checks are not listed.
- **Permissions:** recording and service changes are bench work (result.enter); registering equipment and scheduling checks is configuration (admin.config.edit). Every change is audited.
- **Page:** `/equipment` (Patients & Testing, beside Reagent QC): checks to do with Record; the register with each check's status and last record; out of service and back, warning on return while a check's latest record failed.

### Verification

- Unit: due states by date, never done, failed; each validation.
- Integration: register, schedule, record, due list and next day; duplicate code; failure needs a note and stays failed; out of service off the due list, records after repair, return; check refusals and retirement; the demo's three states.
- Rendered: record a due check; out-of-service details and the return warning.

### Requirements

- URS-BB-751, FRS-BB-869.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-968 to TEST-BB-974.

### Next

- Iteration 709: a home card and shift handoff count for equipment checks to do, and refusing a modification whose device is registered equipment out of service.

### Found and fixed

1. **Accession from the worklist made a second order.** The row's **Accession** opened the chart's new-order form with its specimen section; saving it would have ordered ABO/Rh and the screen again. It now opens the chart's tube accession, which shows "Waiting for a specimen: ORD0024" and links the tube to it on save. Retested: ACC-UAT-001 accessioned and linked to ORD0024 in one step; both tests became resultable.
2. **Panel results shown as stored data.** The worklist's Result column (also the chart Orders tab and the supervisor queue) showed an ABO/Rh as `{"abo":"O","rh":"Positive","version":1,...}`. `ResultValueText.For` now reads ABO/Rh panels as "O+ · Anti-A:0 · …" and subtest panels as their readings. Retested on the live worklist.
3. **"Save incomplete" on a complete ABO/Rh.** The ABO/Rh save prompt's only button read *Save incomplete* although the result is complete and waits only for a second person's verification. It reads **Save for verification**.

### Observed, not changed

- A patient with no recorded transfusion or pregnancy gets the standard (7-day) specimen window; whether unknown history should take the 3-day window is the facility's decision under OCD-002.
- The ABO/Rh entered by one user waits for a different user to verify (correct); the screen was saved and verified by the same user, as configured.

## Iteration 718 — End-user testing pass 2: transfusion request and fulfillment (2026-11-12)

### How it was tested

As the blood bank on the running system with seeded data: Blood orders to prepare → Riley Demo-Multi's surgery order ORD-SURG-DEMO (needed-by passed, tube ACC-DEMO-RCV1 drawn but not received) → receive and accept the tube by scan → order the type and screen → the Ready to issue desk for her held units (crossmatch expired) → repeat crossmatch.

### Found and fixed

1. **Dead end after accepting the tube.** The blood order's next step read "Finish type and screen" and opened an empty Tests tab ("No pending tests on this chart"): no type and screen was ordered on the new tube (the old one, on an expired tube, was complete). The worklist now sees that no test order is linked to the tube and says **Order type and screen on ACC-DEMO-RCV1**, opening the chart's new-order form with the type and screen chosen and the tube selected. Retested: one Save created the order linked to the tube.
2. **"Crossmatch" was not something to click.** On Ready to issue, a unit whose crossmatch expired showed a red Crossmatch badge with nowhere to go. A **Repeat crossmatch** link beside it opens Compatibility with the patient and unit filled in.
3. **An expired crossmatch could not be repeated.** Recording the new crossmatch was refused: "A crossmatch result is already recorded for this unit", although that result had expired with its specimen, so the unit stayed held and unissuable. Only a current compatible result, or any incompatible one, now stands. The crossmatch is recorded on the specimen chosen on screen (it had silently used the order's first linked specimen), and a specimen not linked to the order is refused by name: "Specimen ACC-DEMO-RCV1 is not linked to order ORD0023. Link it on the order (it needs a completed type and screen), then record the crossmatch." Retested live with that message.

### Not completed in this pass

- The ABO/Rh on the new tube waits for a second user's verification (correct), so the order could not be linked, crossmatched and issued as one user; issuing and bedside documentation are carried to the next pass with a unit already crossmatched.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-996, TEST-BB-997. Full suite passed.

### Next

- Pass 3: issue and bedside, transfusion reaction, mother/baby, QC, interfaces.

## Iteration 719 — End-user testing pass 3: bedside and transfusion reaction (2026-11-12)

### How it was tested

As the ward and the blood bank on the running system with seeded data: Issued units → Riley Demo-Multi's W0001230009205 → Start at the bedside (wristband MRN and DOB, bag scan, second verifier) → finish with the transfusion stopped at 120 mL and a suspected reaction → the reaction investigation and its report.

### Found and fixed

1. **No vital signs at the bedside, so no baseline for a reaction.** The transfusion record had vitals fields (one marked "placeholder") that nothing filled, and the bedside form did not ask. A febrile reaction is judged from the temperature rise over the baseline, and the workup had neither. The bedside form now takes optional vitals before the start and after the end (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate); a mistyped value is refused (plausibility only, no clinical limits; none is required, consistent with the earlier decision not to invent required vitals). The reaction case and its report show "Before: T 36.9 °C · P 84 · BP 128/74 · RR 18 · After: T 38.6 °C · P 112 · BP 132/78 · Temperature +1.7 °C from before the transfusion". Retested live end to end: start with vitals, stop with vitals and a suspected reaction, investigation #2 opened, vitals on the case and the report.

### Raised for decision

- **OCD-084:** the bedside second-verifier picker lists, and the server accepts, any active account (billing, auditor, read-only viewer). Who may verify at the bedside is the facility's policy; nothing changed pending the decision.

### Observed working

- The start was refused until a second verifier was chosen from the user directory (typed text is not accepted).
- A suspected reaction opened the investigation and held the patient's next unit until a reason and the physician who decided to continue were recorded (OCD-078).

### Tests

- TEST-BB-998, TEST-BB-999. Full suite passed.

### Next

- Pass 4: mother/baby, QC (reagent and equipment) and interfaces (HL7, instruments).

## Iteration 720 — End-user testing pass 4: mother/baby, reagent QC, instrument interface (2026-11-12)

### How it was tested

On the running system with seeded data: Baby Girl Maya (MRN0027) and her mother (MRN0025) → the RhIG list → RhIG given for the mother; Reagent QC worklist → daily QC for anti-A lot AA-24117; the ImmuLINK Echo simulator → Group and Screen results for Riley Demo-Multi's tube ACC-DEMO-RCV1 → the instrument log, the stored message and its rule trace, and the bench worklist.

### Found and fixed

1. **Every positive reaction from the analyzer posted as 1+.** The Echo sent anti-A 2+ and B cells 4+; the worklist showed 1+ for both. The rule trace showed the seeded score-to-grade rules ("Numeric 1 to 1+": `>= 1 AND < 20`) matching "2+": the rule engine compared a value that is not a number with a number as text ("2+" sorts between "1" and "20"), and a real score (50 → 3+) was then re-converted by the next rule to 1+. A value that is not a number now never matches a comparison with a number; text compared with text is unchanged. Retested live: a resend posted anti-A 3+ and B cells 1+ exactly as sent.
2. **Two anti-D readings, one shown.** The Echo reports Anti-D1 and Anti-D2; both translate to the panel's Anti-D, and the second silently replaced the first, so a split (0 and 2+, the pattern that prompts a weak or partial D investigation) would not reach the verifier. When two readings for one subtest differ, the result now carries "Anti-D1 0 / Anti-D2 2+ → Anti-D 2+" beside its source as an instrument flag. Which reading counts, or whether to hold, is not decided by the software.

### Observed working

- The analyzer's ABO/Rh (A negative) against the O positive on file was flagged Discrepancy and left pending verification; the panel reads as reactions, not stored data.
- The infant's chart names the mother and her type; the neonatal rules stay off until validation script S-14 (OCD-074).
- RhIG given was recorded on the mother's evaluation; reagent QC Passed follows Expected and Observed, with a warning on a mismatch.

### Gaps carried to the next pass

- **RhIG lot is free text:** not checked against RhIG received or its expiry, so a typo or an expired lot is accepted and a lot recall could miss a recipient.
- **Daily reagent QC one lot at a time:** seven entries each morning; no single daily QC table.
- **HL7 interface** not exercised in this pass.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-1000 to TEST-BB-1002.

### Next

- Pass 5: an RhIG lot register (lot, product, expiry) checked when RhIG is given; then HL7 and daily QC entry.

## Iteration 742 — End-user testing pass 26: reagent QC after a failure (2026-11-12)

### How it was tested

On the running system with seeded data: Reagent QC, with the seeded Anti-D lot AD-24092 whose QC failed today (3+ expected, 0 observed). Opened its 5 results to review, then recorded a passing repeat QC (3+ / 3+).

### Found and fixed

1. **A passing repeat QC cleared the review.** Results to review were counted only while the lot's latest QC was failed, so the repeat QC would have dropped the five ABO/Rh results tested with the anti-D lot since it last passed from the worklist, the lookback and the shift handoff, unreviewed. The review period now runs from the last passed QC before a failure to the first passed QC after it; a lot that has passed again stays on the worklist as **Review results** with its count until each result is marked reviewed. Retested live: after the passing repeat, AD-24092 showed "Review results … 5 results to review", the five still marked To review.

3. The lookback's banner said "This lot's latest QC failed" after the repeat passed; it now says the lot failed QC and that a passing repeat does not clear the results.

### Checked, not defects

- The worklist's "Enter QC5 results to review" is two buttons ("Enter QC", "5 results to review") read as one line; the reagents' "Used for tests" are editable fields (ABORH, ABSC, DAT, XM are set).

On the running system with seeded data: the unidentified trauma chart UNK-20261108-01 and its identify step; the mother and baby link of Maya DEMO-RHIG and Baby Girl Maya, and Noor DEMO-RHIG's delivery evaluation; Issue & Transfuse › Second ABO/Rh due › Order ABO/Rh for Nora Kline.

### Checked, not defects

- Identifying the unidentified chart asks for the identified patient's MRN and how they were identified, and merges the temporary chart into theirs (warning of units issued under the temporary identity); an MRN with no chart is refused with "register the identified patient first".
- Baby Girl Maya is linked to Maya DEMO-RHIG (MRN0025); Noor DEMO-RHIG's delivery evaluation records an Rh-positive infant without an infant chart.

### Found and fixed

1. **An order defaulted to the wrong ordering location.** Nora Kline's visit is on 6E Oncology, which is not an ordering location; the form said so but had chosen the first location on the list, Emergency Department. When the visit's place matches no ordering location, none is chosen now ("Choose the ordering location"); saving without one is refused.
2. **The second ABO/Rh order defaulted to the same tube.** Order ABO/Rh from Second ABO/Rh due opened the order with "Auto-link most recent accepted specimen": with a current specimen, the second type would have been run on the same tube, which does not count. It now starts with "Accession a new specimen now".

Retested live on Nora Kline's chart (nothing saved).

### Tests

- Page changes (inspection). Full suite passed.

1. **"Today" turned over at 19:00 Eastern.** A patient's age at the issue gate (childbearing potential for emergency release), the date-of-birth check, an RhIG lot's expiry on receipt, an outside antibody report's date, and ISBT product-code retirement compared with the UTC date, so from 19:00 Eastern a lot expiring that day was refused as expired and a code retired the next day was already retired. They now use the facility's day, as equipment and reagent QC have since passes 35–36. Retested: a lot expiring 2026-11-12 is received at 20:00 Chicago time and refused on the UTC day (test); the pages load with the services' new settings.

### Remaining

- Admin defaults for a retirement date (compatibility rules, auto-thaw product codes) still take the UTC date.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-1080. Full suite passed.

## Iteration 790 — End-user testing pass 73: deviation investigation (2026-11-14)

### How it was tested

On the running system with seeded data: Deviations (three open: a unit on the wrong shelf, two storage temperature excursions), Update on each.

### Found and fixed

1. **No root cause or reportability.** A deviation could record only a status and a corrective action. A blood bank's deviation must also record why it happened and whether it is reportable to the FDA as a biological product deviation (BPDR, 21 CFR 606.171), with when and under what number it was reported. These are now recorded on Update, audited, and shown in the list ("FDA reportability not determined" until decided). Whether a determination is required to close is OCD-090. Retested live: deviation #1's root cause saved and shown; choosing Reportable offers the report date and number.

### Left in the development data

- Deviation #1: root cause "Test entry: unit returned to the wrong shelf during the count" (test text); reportability not determined.

### Tests

- TEST-BB-1084. Full suite passed.
